subject: sub-010
reason: Source-to-sensor projection is independently consistent in all three sub-010 recordings; sub-003 remains excluded from mechanistic fitting because its release representations disagree.
split: Fit first 60% of run-01; evaluate final 20% after a 50-sample embargo. This is reused development data, not a new confirmatory test.
input_boundary: Fitting process may read anatomy and run-01 SEEG only; an open audit hook rejects source trajectories and generator parameter paths. Evaluator reads parameters only after choices are saved.
initialization: Approximate independent-source covariance C_y=G diag(q) G^T; infer q>=0 with fixed column-normalized ridge 0.001. Match each q to the closest independent-node Epileptor library variance.
prior_provenance: Small declared grid informed by inspected VEC author code a99c883 and earlier development, not loaded from sub-010 generator files; investigator has prior development exposure, so this is not blinded research.
selection: Each network gets the same four candidate simulations; choose lowest Frobenius relative sensor covariance error on training observations. No test or generator scores select candidates.
outputs: Fresh-seed sensor covariance/std errors against the development test block, independent-source fit residual, x0 recovery error evaluated separately, comparison against training-feature persistence.
limitations: Stationary covariance fitting ignores timing and source correlations; inverse projection is underdetermined; no posterior uncertainty or intervention optimization. Failure of basic observation prediction prevents using this fit for therapy planning.
additional_validation_amendment: After fit selection, compare the same saved fresh-seed sensor outputs against sub-010 run-02 and run-03 on channels shared with run-01. No new fit or simulation. Record generator differences only in the evaluator. This exploratory addition was specified after seeing training-fit results and the first within-recording evaluation rows; it is not confirmatory.
resource_limit: One existing GCP CPU thread; within shared 3600-second development-v2 cap and 48-call ceiling. No new data or intervention runs.
